newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine plans to boost maize sowing in 1997-Ag Min.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine plans to boost maize sowing in 1997-Ag Min.

text.p: Ukraine plans to increase maize sowing this year in an effort to boost its livestock market, the deputy prime minister of agriculture said on Friday.
"Without corn we cannot increase our livestock," Mykhailo Zubets told a conference of independent agriculture businesses.
Zubets, also the agriculture minister, said the former Soviet republic would increase sowing to two million hectares this year, from 330,000 hectares sown last year.
Last year's area yielded a maize harvest of 1.8 million tonnes, compared to 2.2 million tonnes in 1995.
Some of Zubets' announcements on plans to reform Ukraine's farm sector have left Western agriculture analysts baffled.
Zubets, an academic with a livestock specialisation, has been criticised by analysts for favouring Soviet methods of adminstration in a sector which has been slow to reform to market principles.
He did not provide figures on how much livestock Ukraine produces.
The minister added that collective farms would be employed in the effort to boost maize production, and that commercial companies would also be "encouraged" to partake in the effort.
